title: 2026-03-04-rivergrove-bank-data-residency-discovery
summary: Intro discovery on data residency and compliance for planned LLM use cases. Customer weighs Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for EU/US data residency, encryption/KMS, logging retention, SOC2/HIPAA needs. Agreed next steps: send security pack, schedule technical deep dive for Private deployment and pilot scope, share SSO/SAML diagram and initial pricing estimate.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
next_steps: Maya Chen - Send Redwood security pack + SOC2/ISO docs by 2026-03-06
Lucas Patel - Schedule technical deep dive for Private deployment and network diagram week of 2026-03-09
Maya Chen - Share initial pricing estimate for Dedicated reserve and Hosted fallback by 2026-03-08
James Avery - Provide sample dataset and compliance checklist for pilot by 2026-03-11
action_items: Maya Chen - Share SOC2 and ISO paperwork (link) - due 2026-03-06
Lucas Patel - Follow up with Private deployment network diagram and VPC peering notes - due 2026-03-10

meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-04 | Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, i'm the ae on the account, with me today is lucas our solutions engineer. quick roll call?
00:08 James Avery: jim avery here, chief info security officer at rivergrove bank.
00:12 Monica Reyes: monica reyes, head of data.
00:15 Ethan Cole: ethan cole, devops lead.
00:17 Priya Shah: priya from procurement. thanks.
00:20 Maya Chen: great, appreciate it. the goal for today's call is to understand your residency and compliance constraints and walk through how redwood's hosted, dedicated and private options map to those controls. not a product demo per se.
00:32 Lucas Patel: quick note, i'll be the technical person, so i'll jump in on network and kms questions.
: --
02:10 Maya Chen: can you share a bit about the project, where you're planning to use llm features and what data flows through it?
02:22 Monica Reyes: sure. we're building a customer support assistant and automated document summarization for account agreements. those docs contain pii, some ssns historically, financial transaction details, and certain eu customer records. so data residency is a big one.
02:36 James Avery: from a controls perspective we need audit logs, we need retention controls, SSO integration, and we have to prove where data is physically stored for regulators.
02:47 Maya Chen: understood. when you say eu customer records, do you require that the model inference for eu records be processed in eu-only infrastructure?
02:55 Monica Reyes: yes, gdpr says we need to avoid transferring personal data outside the eu unless we have adequate safeguards. prefer processing inside eu regions.
03:06 Lucas Patel: ok, so that steers toward either hosted with region pinned to eu or a dedicated/private deployment in eu. quick tradeoff: hosted offers fastest time to value and we can guarantee region-based routing for data in our hosted eu region, but customers often want dedicated or private for stronger isolation and audit controls.
03:28 Ethan Cole: what's the difference operationally for us? we run on aws, and we have vins yeah vpc peering etc.
03:35 Lucas Patel: for dedicated, you get reserved gpu pools that are still managed by redwood but isolated to your tenant; network-wise we support private peering and strict egress rules. for private, we deliver a customer-managed control plane — can be deployed in your vpc or on-prem, you manage the infrastructure and keys. both can satisfy residency but private gives you the most control.
03:54 James Avery: what about logs? we can't have raw transcripts retained by vendors beyond X days and we need redaction options.
04:02 Maya Chen: good point. hosted by default retains short-term logs for operational debugging; we can configure retention windows and purge policies. dedicated customers can set stricter retention or opt for no transcript retention. private deployments give you full control over logs — they never leave your network unless you configure external sinks.
04:22 Monica Reyes: do you support bring-your-own-key for encryption? we have an on-prem hsm we want to use for sensitive keys.
04:29 Lucas Patel: yes, BYOK is supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports KMS integrations in certain regions but not direct on-prem HSMs — for absolute separation you'd pick Private and plug in your HSM/KMS.
04:40 Priya Shah: curious on certification posture — we are subject to ffiec guidances and also have clients asking about hipaa for some treasury services. do you have SOC2? hipaa attestation?
04:51 Maya Chen: redwood is SOC 2 type II. we also provide a HIPAA-eligible product and execute BAA for covered workloads; we'll send our security pack that includes SOC2 report, ISO certs, and our hipaa controls map.
05:03 James Avery: will want to see the actual artefacts, yes. also curious about data residency proofs — like location attestations.
05:11 Lucas Patel: we keep deployment region metadata and can provide audit logs showing model inference executed in eu-west1 etc. with dedicated / private you get more granular provenance.
05:24 Monica Reyes: ok, another question — model weights and fine-tuning: do weights leave our region, or do you host fine-tune artifacts in your global storage?
05:33 Lucas Patel: by default model artifacts are in the region where inference runs. for hosted models in multi-region setups, weights may be replicated for performance; with dedicated you can choose region-scoped model stores; with private, you control storage location entirely. if you have strict data residency, private or dedicated region-scoped is recommended.
05:50 Ethan Cole: network ports and firewall rules for private deploy — what's required?
05:55 Lucas Patel: typical egress for control plane and metrics, but for private we can operate with minimal outbound, and we support VPC peering and private endpoints. i'll share a network diagram and list of ports.
06:08 Priya Shah: procurement question — what's the typical timeline to go from discovery to pilot for dedicated vs private?
06:15 Maya Chen: hosted pilot can start in days. dedicated pilot usually a few weeks for capacity reservation and access. private can be 4-8 weeks depending on on-prem changes and security approvals.
06:28 James Avery: for gdpr, we may need processor agreements and SCCs. do you provide standard clauses or work with legal?
06:36 Maya Chen: yes we provide DPA with SCCs, and for enterprise we can negotiate addenda.
06:42 Monica Reyes: about logging again — we need token-level redaction; we can't have customer tokens or account numbers stored in logs, can you do PII redaction?
06:51 Lucas Patel: we have structured logging and PII extraction hooks; can redact or hash tokens prior to persistence. with private deployment you can implement redaction on your side as well before logs hit storage.
07:05 James Avery: HIPAA — does redwood sign a BAA and have controls for ePHI?
07:11 Maya Chen: yes, we have a BAA for covered deployments; we will include the BAA template in the security pack.
07:18 Monica Reyes: ok, let's talk about fallbacks and graceful degradation. if we put primary inference in eu hosted region and it fails, what's the fallback policy? do we ever route to us?
07:28 Lucas Patel: routing policies are configurable. we support strict-region policies that prevent cross-region failover. default hosted fallback may use nearest available region which could be outside eu; for compliance you can set 'region strict' to prevent cross-border processing. note that this may affect availability.
07:45 Ethan Cole: happy to accept availability trade-offs if it keeps us compliant.
07:48 James Avery: encryption at rest and in transit — standard?
07:51 Lucas Patel: TLS 1.2+, and AES-256 for data at rest. BYOK with HSM is available for dedicated/private.
08:00 Priya Shah: do you keep raw audio or transcripts? not relevant for us, but asking — for call centers, some customers want retention disabled.
08:09 Maya Chen: retention disabled is available for private and configurable for dedicated; hosted has default retention for metrics and short-term traces but can be minimized per agreement.
8:18 Monica Reyes: sample question — can we run the model weights in our environment and only use redwood for orchestration?
08:25 Lucas Patel: sort of — private allows you to run the runtime in your environment; you can bring your own model weights and still use redwood's control plane if desired. there's some nuance about licensing for certain open models.
08:38 James Avery: what about third party subprocessors? need to know all vendors with access to data.
08:44 Maya Chen: we'll include a subprocessors list in the pack; for private deployments subprocessors are minimal because most services run in your environment.
09:00 Monica Reyes: on metrics — we need token-level cost info but not PII. can we get anonymized token billing?
09:06 Lucas Patel: yes, billing can be tokenized and de-identified. we provide cost dashboards and per-route breakdowns without PII.
09:18 Priya Shah: procurement — pricing model for dedicated vs private? is private a license + infra?
09:23 Maya Chen: yes private is typically a platform license + support; dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit; hosted is usage. i'll share a starter pricing sheet.
09:35 James Avery: i'd like to propose a pilot that handles eu PII in eu region using either dedicated or private. what's the recommended starting point?
09:44 Lucas Patel: if you want minimal lift but strict residency, start with dedicated region-scoped capacity in eu. if you need full control over keys and no vendor data retention, choose private. for a pilot, dedicated is often faster.
10:00 Monica Reyes: are there any limitations on model types in private? like can we run quantized models or older tensor runtimes?
10:07 Lucas Patel: private exposes the same runtime with options for quantization; some experimental kernels might require additional configuration but generally same feature set.
10:18 Ethan Cole: let's talk about support SLAs for dedicated — latency and uptime guarantees?
10:24 Maya Chen: we have SLA tiers for dedicated customers, with guaranteed uptime and latency targets depending on commit level; we'll include SLA PDFs.
10:33 James Avery: curious on documentation — do you have audit log schema and sample log extracts?
10:38 Lucas Patel: yes, i'll attach sample audit logs, fields include request id, region, model, start/end timestamps, optionally anonymized prompt hash, and decision provenance.
10:50 Monica Reyes: okay good. can we see an example of redaction pipeline?
10:54 Lucas Patel: i'll include that in the tech deep dive.
11:00 Priya Shah: on procurement timelines, we need to align legal and security review; might take 4-6 weeks post pilot to finalize contract.
11:07 Maya Chen: understood.
11:10 James Avery: last detail — data subject requests under gdpr: will you assist with retrieval or deletion requests if data processed by redwood?
11:18 Maya Chen: yes we provide APIs and support to handle dsr; for private deployments you control the data store and process dsr internally. for hosted/dedicated we help with DSR workflows and provide deletion endpoints per DPA.
11:30 Monica Reyes: ok, that helps.
11:36 Maya Chen: could we recap concrete next steps?
11:40 James Avery: we want the security pack and SOC2 and HIPAA/Baa template; we'd like a technical deep dive targeted at private deployment network and KMS; pricing estimate for dedicated eu region; and we'll provide sample data checklist.
11:58 Maya Chen: perfect. i'll send the security pack and pricing, lucas will own the tech deep dive. we'll aim to schedule the deep dive for the week of march 9th.
12:12 Lucas Patel: i'll send network diagram and port list, plus sample audit logs and a redaction pipeline doc.
12:20 Priya Shah: procurement will review pricing and come back with questions.
12:25 James Avery: thanks all.
12:27 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts. bye.
12:30 [call ends]
